rationale: History: baseline 128x64x64 s1 t256 sw0=3560.55us; 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw64=3518.99us; 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw64=2504.88us; 64x128x32 s2 t256 sw64=3989.52us; 32x256x32 s1 t64 sw64=2891.16us; 32x256x32 s1 t128 sw32=2503.47us (BEST, 278.9MB DRAM, 3 blocks/SM); 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw32=3443.78us; 64x128x64 s1 t128 sw64=2715.84us; 32x256x32 s1 t256 sw16=3450.96us. Lessons: threads=128 decisively dominates 64/256 at the winning wide-N tile (3 blocks/SM vs 2), so threads is fixed to {128} to stop wasting rounds on tied thread costs; block_N=256 with small block_M=32 and block_K=32 at s1 is the anchored family; block_K>=64 and block_M=64 regressed; stage>=2 regressed. Prior rounds repeatedly re-selected the excluded 32x256x32/s1 family, so here I admit block_M=16 (small-M occupancy with wide-N, previously untested at t128) plus block_M 32/64, keep block_N>=128 (32 dropped as low-N), block_K={32,64} (128 dropped as regressed), num_stages={1,2} (3-4 repeatedly regressed or tied), and swizzle={4,8,16,64} to test untested smaller panels alongside the best panel 64 while skipping the already-tested 0/32. Weights unchanged: traffic=2 (DRAM cuts tracked latency), launches=0.5 (4096^2 grid saturates), pipeline=1 (stage benefit unproven), footprint=1 to keep estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N) under the hard 32768 cap. Next hypothesis: does block_M=16 with block_N=256, block_K=32, s1, t128 plus swizzle 4/8/16 beat the 2503.47us best, or does swizzle=64 remain tied-best? If 16 wins, refine around it; if not, drop block_M=16 and next probe swizzle behavior at block_N=128 to test whether wide-N is truly required. Scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR but do NOT execute the CUDA binary; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
